explanation: Array.prototype.sort() with no comparator function coerces every element to a string and sorts lexicographically, not numerically. For an array like [10, 2, 1], the string comparison yields ['1','10','2'], so the result is [1, 10, 2] instead of the intended [1, 2, 10]. The fix is to pass an explicit comparator like (a, b) => a - b.
prompt: This function is supposed to sort numbers ascending. What's the bug?
choices: sort() with no comparator converts elements to strings and compares them lexicographically, breaking numeric order for multi-digit numbers
sort() mutates the original array instead of returning a new one, which is always wrong here
The function should use a for loop instead of calling sort()
sort() throws a TypeError when the array contains more than two elements
